description: A rename (BATCH_WINDOW -> BATCH_WINDOW_SECONDS) migrated metrics.py but left producer.py and consumer.py importing and using the old name: ImportError at import time in both. This is the shape ADR-0013's `group` exists for — ONE defect that a Finding cannot express, because a finding names one path and one line (ADR-0009's addendum C), so the reviewer has to file two and SAY they are one fix. Both defective lines are inside diff hunks (the PR adds a docstring above each), so both are anchorable and neither can be demoted to residual_risk: the question that decides is 'could I confirm it?', and an ImportError from a name that demonstrably no longer exists is confirmed. metrics.py is the control — it was migrated correctly, so a finding against it is a false positive.
grouping_note: grouped_paths asserts BOTH directions, which is what makes one key enough: the two findings share a group, AND no finding outside them carries it. The second half is load-bearing — a model that puts every finding in group 1 satisfies the first half trivially, and that answer is worse than no grouping, since it renders a cross-reference between unrelated defects and invites a commander to remediate them together. A bare count was the alternative and is rejected: pinned exactly it goes red the moment a run finds a legitimate extra defect (the padding case provenance_boundary_adjacent_bug's max_findings note already pays for), and pinned as a ceiling it detects no collapse. Stated as PATHS, never ordinals: the model's order is not the rendered order (rendered_findings sorts by severity), which is exactly why post.render composes the cross-reference rather than the model. Graded at FINDING granularity, not path: keyed on the path, the first half was an intersection of per-path group SETS and so was satisfied by any one finding per path agreeing, which let the two halves sit in DIFFERENT groups with a third finding on a wanted path bridging them — and the second half exempts wanted paths, so neither half could see it. The harness then renders a cross-reference coupling the bridging note with one half while the real other half gets none. constants.py is deliberately NOT in grouped_paths, so this scenario measures a willingness to UNDER-group: a reviewer who also files the root-cause finding there in the same group fails via the strays half, even though all three lines are one rename and that is arguably the most honest grouping. Adding it was measured and is worse — grouped_paths requires a finding on every path it names, and no measured run files one on constants.py (12/12 across 3 runs, 2026-08-10, all grouping producer+consumer), so the answer the reviewer actually gives would fail. That is plan_multi_file_fix's failure mode exactly: a fixture no achievable answer satisfies, grading the model wrong for the fixture's shape. Accepted with the cost stated rather than traded for an unsatisfiable assertion. If a run ever fails on a same-group constants.py finding, the fixture is what is wrong, not the reviewer.
line_accuracy_note: Exact line 8 in both files: `deadline = clock() + BATCH_WINDOW` and `since = clock() - BATCH_WINDOW`. The import on line 1 of each file is NOT in a hunk (the diff's window starts at 4), so anchoring to the import rejects on provenance — which is correct and is why the use site is the anchor. The two files' hunks are identical in shape, so a file-attribution slip lands on a coincidentally-valid line in the other file and only the two findings_any entries catch it.
max_findings_note: 3, not 2: metrics.py's migration is correct but a model may reasonably note the missing test for MAX_BATCH_ITEMS, which is a real prompt category. Room for one such finding without letting the artifact pad.
